request.spec:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added an "Export claims as CSV" button (`data-testid="export-claims"`) next to the existing people export, and all 4 Playwright tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

The file starts with the header `person,number,date,amount,due,status,period`, then has one line per claim:
- **Order:** people in list order, each person's claims oldest first. Retired people are included even when "Show retired" is off.
- **Figures as on screen:** the due is worked out the same way the claim row works it out, so it shows `n/a` when there's no rate. A draft's number and a claim outside any period are left empty.
- **Format:** it uses the same quoting function and `\n` line ends as the people export.

The change is only in the front end, in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`. The server and stored data weren't touched, since everything the export needs is already loaded on the page. I also moved the download step into a small `download()` helper that both exports now use, so the people export now goes through it too. The file downloads as `claims-<sheet id>.csv`.
